title: Potential Problems with Sampling
rights: Original public teacher-authored practice; no secure homework or copied assessment questions.

items.prompt: A properly selected random sample has a sample mean below the population mean. What is the best conclusion?
items.hint: Think about what one sample can establish.
items.solution: A single randomly chosen sample can deviate by chance; this fact alone does not demonstrate systematic bias.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: B
options.text: Sampling variability can produce a difference without bias.

items.prompt: A city samples uniformly from a landline-only phone directory. What is a likely threat?
items.hint: Some eligible residents have no chance to be sampled.
items.solution: People without landlines are not in the sampling frame, so they cannot be selected.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A researcher randomly selects 100 students. Twenty selected students never answer. What issue needs attention?
items.hint: They were selected first, then failed to answer.
items.solution: The 20 nonrespondents were chosen but yielded no observations. If they differ from respondents, estimates may be biased.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: An open online poll receives 10,000 responses. Which statement is most defensible?
items.hint: Who decided which people would be included?
items.solution: Volunteers choose whether to join, and respondents may differ from the whole population. Direction cannot be concluded just from sample size.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: It is necessarily unbiased because n is large.

options.label: B
options.text: It is an SRS because anyone may join.

options.label: C
options.text: A large number alone does not repair volunteer self-selection.

options.label: D
options.text: The estimate must be too high.

items.prompt: There are 40 ten-minute walkers and 60 thirty-minute bus riders. Find the population mean commute time in minutes.
items.hint: Compute a weighted mean of all 100 people.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A school obtains a complete roster and selects students at random, but asks: 'You agree our brilliant new schedule helps, right?' Identify a possible bias and a correction.
items.hint: Random selection does not guarantee neutral measurements.
items.solution: The leading wording creates potential **response bias**, even with a complete random frame. Use a neutral, balanced question such as 'Which schedule do you prefer: the new schedule, the previous schedule, or neither?'
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026
items.rubric: Identify the mechanism and justify in context, then give an appropriate correction when requested.

items.prompt: A roster excludes online students. Later, 12 selected students do not answer the survey. Identify two different problems and when they occur.
items.hint: Separate the sampling frame from the response stage.
items.solution: **Undercoverage** happens before selection because online students cannot enter the sample. **Nonresponse** happens after selection because 12 selected students are not observed. Both can affect a study.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026
items.rubric: Identify the mechanism and justify in context, then give an appropriate correction when requested.

items.prompt: In a population of 40 ten-minute walkers and 60 thirty-minute bus riders, a gate survey measures all 40 walkers and gets 10 minutes. Explain why increasing the walker sample from 10 to 40 does not solve the problem.
items.hint: More data from the wrong group cannot represent people excluded by design.
items.solution: The frame excludes all 60 bus riders. Every sampled walker has a 10-minute commute, while the population mean is 22. The downward gap of 12 minutes remains because the systematic exclusion is not repaired. Draw a probability sample from the **complete** roster instead, with neutral measurement and nonresponse follow-up.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026
items.rubric: Identify the mechanism and justify in context, then give an appropriate correction when requested.
